one_month_reasoning: No Snowflake earnings in the window: Q3 FY27 (quarter ending Oct 31) has not been dated by the company; Q3 FY26 was reported 2025-12-03, so early December, after 2026-10-30. In-window events: the $3.75B 0% convertible closes Oct 1 (convert-arb hedging largely already in the ~4% drop on Sep 28; the $548M repurchase of in-the-money 2027 notes also unwinds some old hedges, roughly neutral); a possible ruling on the motion to dismiss in the older securities class action and the Oct 13 MTD filing in the newer one (small); hyperscaler Q3 prints in late October (AWS +37%, Azure +43%, GCP +82% last quarter per the companies' own releases, so the bar is high but the consumption backdrop is strong); the Oct 28 FOMC, where hike odds fell to ~36% after the cooler Sep 30 PCE print, so rate risk is two-sided and smaller than feared. Post-earnings drift after a beat-and-raise is a mild positive, the software de-rating a mild negative. Net: close to neutral, lognormal around ~$336 with monthly vol ~17.5% (62%/3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend of EV/NTM revenue (Sep-2027 NTM revenue ~$9.6B x 13.5x, 50%), EV/NTM adjusted FCF (~$2.4B x 43x, 25%) and P/E on FY29 non-GAAP EPS (~$4.45 x 72x, 25%), with ~$2.0B Sep-2027 net cash and ~388M diluted shares, giving ~$317 per share one year out.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 total ~$6.35B; FY28 ~+28-30% to ~$8.1-8.2B (consensus $8.11B per supervisor review); FY29 ~+25%; NTM Oct-27..Sep-28 ~$9.5-9.8B. Hyperscaler growth now verified at source (AWS +37%, Azure +43%, GCP +82%) supports ~30% near-term consumption growth; MongoDB Atlas ~29% corroborates.

Cut from 14x per supervisor. Peer line on Sep-30 data: Datadog EV $93B on LTM $4.2B = 22x LTM, ~18x NTM at 24% growth; MongoDB ~9.8x LTM, ~8x NTM at 19%; SNOW ~20x LTM, ~15.5x NTM today. A mid/high-20s grower with 126% NRR sits between MDB and DDOG, ~13x; I keep a 0.5x premium over the supervisor's 13x centre because DDOG at similar growth trades far above the 'DDOG ~10.6x' the supervisor used, but below 14x because Databricks' warehousing product ($1.5B run-rate, >100%) competes directly with SNOW's core.

Pro forma today ~$1.3-1.6B: Jul-31 cash+investments $4.33B + ~$3.71B net proceeds - $0.38B capped calls - $0.55B repurchase of in-the-money 2027 notes (~$0.26B face) vs ~$5.8B face debt. Add ~$1.5-1.8B adj. FCF less ~$0.65B/yr RSU tax withholding and buybacks -> ~$2.0B (was ~$3B in round 1).

Q3 FY27 non-GAAP diluted guide 382M; ~2% net SBC dilution; old 2024 notes' excess shares ~5M after capped calls ($157.50-$225) already partly in the guide; new notes convert at $484/$500, out of the money in base case.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM adjusted FCF at Sep-2027 ~$2.4B x 43x = $103.2B + $2.0B net cash = $105.2B / 388M

inputs_detail.derivation: Lowered from 45x: GAAP SBC is ~27% of revenue (10-Q Note 12 via supervisor), so adjusted FCF overstates owner FCF and cash is largely absorbed by RSU tax withholding and buybacks; 43x (~2.3% yield) aligns with a 13.5x sales multiple at ~25% margin after that haircut.
FY29 revenue ~$10.3B x ~19% non-GAAP operating margin = ~$1.95B, slightly lower interest income given ~$1B less net cash, ~20% tax -> ~$1.73B / 388M shares.
Consistent with ~13.5x EV/sales at ~19% operating margin; a cross-check since high-growth software on early-stage margins trades on sales.

bear.story: AI consumption step-up proves lumpy; Databricks (>$7B run-rate, >80%, and its warehousing product at $1.5B+ growing >100%, company PR Aug-2026) takes new SQL/AI workloads; SNOW growth slides to low 20s by FY28 guide and the multiple compresses to ~8x NTM sales amid a software de-rating.

base.story: Growth glides from 37% to high-20s, NRR stays low-to-mid 120s, margins expand ~2pts/yr; multiple compresses from ~15.5x to ~13-13.5x NTM sales, offset by ~30% revenue growth; stock roughly flat.

bull.story: Hyperscaler acceleration (AWS +37%, Azure +43%, GCP +82%) keeps data consumption strong, CoCo/CoWork AI products drive consolidation; growth holds 33%+ through FY28 and the market keeps ~16-17x on ~$10B NTM revenue, near DDOG's current NTM multiple.

thesis_break_reason: ~36% below today and below the pre-Q2 range; at ~$215 the market would be pricing growth in the low 20s or a Databricks share-loss story (NRR toward 115%) rather than 60%-vol noise. An FY28 product-revenue guide well below ~28% or a sharp drop in $1M+ customer adds would confirm it.

reasoning: Industry lane. Round 2 verifies the value-chain numbers at source: AWS +37% ($42.2B), Azure +43%, Google Cloud +82% ($24.8B, $514B backlog) all confirmed in the companies' own releases, so the consumption backdrop is genuinely strong. Databricks' own Aug-13 release gives >$7B run-rate, >80% growth, a $190B valuation (~27x run-rate), and, newly relevant, its Lakehouse warehousing product at >$1.5B run-rate growing >100%: direct competition with Snowflake's core, and faster than I assumed. Accepting the supervisor's evidence-based corrections: the convert is $3.75B (conversion $484/$500), net cash is ~$1.3-1.6B today and ~$2.0B by Sep-2027 (not $3B, about -$3/share), GAAP SBC ~27% of revenue. I cut EV/NTM sales from 14x to 13.5x; I do not go all the way to 13x because Sep-30 peer data show Datadog at ~18x NTM on 24% growth (not ~10.6x), while MongoDB is ~8x at 19%, so the midpoint for a mid/high-20s grower with 126% NRR is ~13-13.5x. Methods: EV/sales $339, FCF $271 (43x, SBC haircut), P/E $320 -> blended ~$317 (from $331). Scenarios $180/$340/$510 at 25/50/25 (mean ~$343). Ladder: lognormal-like, median ~$335, sigma ~0.52, slightly fatter left tail for the Databricks and de-rating risk. 1-month ladder essentially neutral; rate risk in the window is smaller after the PCE print.
